dedupe_keys.name: cari 7 and cari 7a flight radiation dose programs faa

description: CARI-7 is a computer program from the FAA Civil Aerospace Medical Institute that calculates the effective dose of galactic cosmic radiation received by an individual on an aircraft, based on an anthropomorphic phantom. It handles waypoint-defined and shortest-route flight paths, accounts for changes in altitude and location during a flight, and can give particle-specific doses along a route or at chosen locations up to 300,000 ft. It covers any flight worldwide and calculations back to 1958 without extra data; monthly averages use databases of geomagnetic field and solar activity effects, and hour-specific runs adjust for geomagnetic storms and Forbush decreases. Atmospheric response databases were generated with the Monte Carlo transport code MCNPX 2.7.0. CARI-7A is the research version with more options, including three atmospheric transport switches, several cosmic ray and solar particle event models and custom input spectra. Both run from a command prompt on most personal computers (about 80 to 100 MB of disc) and are free downloads from the FAA page, last updated on 1 September 2026, with user guides and documentation on cutoff rigidities, particle spectra and atmospheric transport; the FAA also publishes reports on in-flight radiation and a CARI-based solar radiation alert system. Caveats: CARI-7 addresses galactic radiation and is slower with hour-specific options. It supports hazard exposure analysis for aviation crews and passengers during space weather; a related record is the NAIRAS nowcast model.
